title: Oct 8, 2026AnnouncementsBuilding on our commitment to American scientific discovery
summary: Announcements Building on our commitment to American scientific discovery Oct 8, 2026 Anthropic is deepening its support for American scientific research by committing $150 million over three years to the Genesis Mission , a federal initiative to accelerate scientific and technological discovery through AI. The funding will go toward making Claude available to more than 15 agencies that are part of the mission, including NASA, the National Institutes of Health, and the National Science Foundation. We first announced our partnership with the US Department of Energy (DOE) and the Genesis Mission last December . Since then, we have worked with DOE to bring Claude to scientists across the national laboratories. Today, we announced this new commitment as part of the Science: A New Golden Age Summit hosted by the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy in Washington, DC. Supporting American scientists We share the administration’s view, laid out in “ Science: A New Golden Age ,” that AI can have a profound and positive impact on scientific discovery, and we are glad to back its efforts to support American scientists. Researchers at federal agencies and national laboratories work on some of the world’s most difficult scientific problems. Through our commitment, we aim to help them use Claude to meaningfully advance their work. Over the next three years, we will: Provide Claude, Claude Code, and API credits to several hundred Genesis Mission research projects; Partner closely with agencies and national laboratories on the administration’s top science priorities, including fusion energy and quantum computing; and Provide training, onboarding, and technical support to scientists on Genesis Mission projects, and help agencies new to the Genesis Mission get their first projects running. title: Oct 8, 2026AnnouncementsIntroducing the Anthropic Cyber Mission
summary: Announcements Introducing the Anthropic Cyber Mission Oct 8, 2026 Today we’re launching the Anthropic Cyber Mission, a long-term commitment to securing the systems everyone depends on. The Cyber Mission is a new effort to support defenders with tools, research, and resources to secure their software and systems. We’re starting with two areas: Critical infrastructure: Starting with securing the operational technology behind power grids, water systems, and transportation networks, and protecting government systems. Today, we’re introducing the Critical Infrastructure Defense Program (CIDP), which brings frontier models, on-site engineers, and threat research to the defenders that protect operational technology. Open-source software: Finding vulnerabilities and proposing patches in the free, shared code that most software depends on, and hardening the underlying code. Today, we’re launching OSS Scanner , which offers open-source projects regular security scans from our strongest models, for free. Frontier models can be misused to exploit vulnerabilities and conduct cyber operations. Despite best efforts, many areas of technology remain dangerously exposed. State-sponsored adversaries have spent years gaining footholds in these systems, across many sectors, so that they can disrupt them. Defenders of critical infrastructure and the OSS community have decades of security experience but have faced severe resource shortages that are exacerbated by this moment. We are recognizing their expertise in these domains and offering our support. We will also expand the Cyber Mission to release tools, research, and resources in new areas to help secure the world. As part of Project Glasswing , partners uncovered many vulnerabilities, but we haven’t yet achieved a sufficient reduction in cyber risk. title: Networking Startup Eliyan Draws Takeover Interest, Held Early Talks With Arm
summary: Semiconductor M&A has been humming. One of the next deals could be for Eliyan, whose technology allows separate chips inside an AI system to talk to one another more quickly and efficiently.The five-year-old startup, valued at $1 billion in July, has notified some of its investors in the last few days that it received a takeover bid, according to people familiar with the matter. It has been working with an investment bank since the summer and is likely to aim for a valuation of $3 billion, according to some of the people.Softbank-owned Arm, an existing investor, held early talks about potentially buying Eliyan, but it didn’t make a bid and would be unlikely to do so at that valuation, said a person familiar with the matter.

title: Oct 8, 2026Announcements2026 Usage Policy update
summary: Announcements 2026 Usage Policy update Oct 8, 2026 Each year, Anthropic updates its Usage Policy in response to the evolving capabilities of our models, and the feedback we’ve received from our customers. We're publishing a new version of the policy today. In this post, we summarize the changes we’ve made. Most of the updates in the latest version are intended to clarify existing rules. In the year since our last refresh, Claude has taken on longer, more independent work. This update provides new examples that show how our rules apply to Claude’s new capabilities. It draws on new patterns of misuse in influence operations, weapons development, and surveillance that we’ve observed in the past year (as we’ve documented in our latest threat intelligence report ). We’ve also made updates to clarify our requirements for high-risk use cases in areas like health and finance, to add controls for when Claude is used to autonomously take physical actions, and to address abusive behavior toward our models. The updated policy takes effect on November 12. The full Usage Policy and Supported Regions Policy can be found on their respective pages. A new section on deceptive activity As we wrote about last month , we’ve seen examples of state media outlets, government propaganda offices, and commercial firms using Claude to run networks of fake accounts and fabricated news sites. Our policy already prohibited this activity, but the restrictions were scattered across our elections, fraud, privacy, and disinformation sections. We've consolidated those rules into a new section titled Do Not Engage in Deceptive Campaigns or Artificial Activity, which applies to deceptive activity of any kind (whether political or commercial). It covers efforts to obscure who is behind a message or amplify content through fake accounts or posts, along with building the tools and infrastructure for running influence operation campaigns. Refocusing our elections section We’ve refined our political content
title_es: Anthropic prohíbe el comportamiento abusivo hacia Claude

bajada_en: As part of its policy update, Anthropic added a prohibition against sustained abusive or cruel behavior toward Claude. The update also introduces controls for high-risk cases in healthcare and finance.
